notes.quote: Agnes met Theodore in her office
notes.reader_gets: Agnes receives a man named Theodore in her own office.

notes.quote: Agnes met Theodore in her office in an emerald dress with a severe collar
notes.reader_gets: Place and clothing phrases are stacked back to back after both names, so for a moment it is unclear whose outfit it is; context settles it on Agnes.
She wears a one-piece dress, which clashes with the miniskirt and the robe on the hanger in paragraph 2.

notes.quote: cut right up to the throat
notes.reader_gets: The collar rises all the way to her throat.
The collar is austere and strict.

notes.quote: from which straps fell to hold up her full
notes.reader_gets: Straps of the garment run down from the collar and support her breasts.
Her breasts are full, with the fullness then qualified as moderate.
Her figure is judged by good taste, not just by size.

notes.quote: from which straps fell to hold up her full, if tastefully moderate, breasts with their beauty marks
notes.reader_gets: The clause is clear, but the concession is wedged into the adjective stack, the moles trail on afterward, and the relative clause hangs off the collar, so it reads as translated.
Her breasts have small dark moles on them.

notes.quote: whenever Agnes laughed or drew on a cigarette. The magess loved both.
notes.reader_gets: "Both" most naturally picks up the laughing and the smoking that come right before it.
Agnes is a female mage, the profession the Academy trains.
"Both" repeats the previous sentence's "both", so it clearly means the laughing and the smoking she loves.

notes.quote: happened to be doing both just then
notes.reader_gets: At that very moment in the scene she is laughing and smoking.

notes.quote: And Agnes happened to be doing both just then.
notes.reader_gets: A crisp, dry one-line punchline.

notes.quote: Together with the miniskirt, the bronze high-heeled shoes and the golden nails made of melted-down etons, Agnes's look defied every principle of the Academy
notes.reader_gets: With the skirt, heels and nails added, her whole look defies the Academy, though the opener makes the look seem to act alongside its own parts.
Her nails are made from the same currency, etons, that later prices an Academy education.

notes.quote: where students were obliged to wear clothes of regulation colors and cut, and where the Pigsty's drilling in high collars and robes was kept up by resident mages, graduates already, until grey hair and the grave
notes.reader_gets: A long chain of clauses with a stiff clothing phrase, a parenthetical "graduates already" and a trailing time phrase; readable but plainly translated.
The collar-and-robe habit was instilled by military-style drill.
The capital letter makes Pigsty a nickname for the place.
The name plainly means a pen where pigs are kept.
The pig-pen insult is carried by the name itself.

notes.quote: was kept up by resident mages, graduates already
notes.reader_gets: The residents keep the drill going, but it is unclear whether they keep to it in their own dress or impose it on students.
The habit lasts until they go grey.
The habit lasts all the way to the grave.

notes.quote: Agnes's green robe on the hanger
notes.reader_gets: The hanging garment is a robe, the same kind of garment as in the drill.

notes.quote: strewn with sequins that threw the morning sun back across the walls like an emerald disco ball
notes.reader_gets: The sequins throw spots of sunlight across the walls like a disco ball.

notes.quote: could afford to dress as brightly
notes.reader_gets: Her rank gives her the means to bear the cost of dressing this way.
"Any Volevich" sounds like a type or family of flashy people, not one specific, talked-about woman, and the gossipy tone is lost.

notes.quote: Because curators, who were appointed at the end of the fourth circle, held practically boundless power. Because, exams aside,
notes.reader_gets: Two fragments in a row both open with "Because", which reads as translated.

notes.quote: whether a student was worthy of moving on
notes.reader_gets: Curators judge whether a student deserves to advance.

notes.quote: the end of the fourth circle
notes.reader_gets: The stages are "circles", an in-world rank term.

notes.quote: all the way to expulsion or graduation
notes.reader_gets: Their control reaches right to the end of the course, whichever way it ends.

notes.quote: And there were a great, great many juicy rumors about how Agnes, in every way unworthy, had got this important curatorial post.
notes.reader_gets: The gossip comes through, but the existential opener and the flat "had got this important curatorial post" read stiffly rather than as a narrator relishing scandal.
The doubled intensifier gives the breathless voice of gossip.
She is judged wholly unworthy, the same measure curators apply to students.

notes.quote: A battle magess and a veteran, Agnes didn't even hold a diploma from the fifth circle, and by rumor she hadn't served out her ten years as a battle magess either.
notes.reader_gets: The facts are clear, but "by rumor" is not idiomatic and the repeated "battle magess" is clunky, so the sentence reads as translated.

notes.quote: didn't even hold a diploma from the fifth circle
notes.reader_gets: She lacks even the minimum fifth-circle diploma.

notes.quote: hadn't served out her ten years as a battle magess either
notes.reader_gets: "Either" marks the service rumour as a further failing.

notes.quote: by rumor she hadn't served out her ten years
notes.reader_gets: The unfinished service is attributed to rumour.

notes.quote: Agnes didn't even hold a diploma from the fifth circle
notes.reader_gets: The missing diploma is stated as fact, outside the rumour.

notes.quote: hadn't served out her ten years
notes.reader_gets: She did not complete her ten-year term.
"Served out" and "her" mark the ten years as a fixed term she owed.
The orgy is set in the offices of the Academy's head.
Two further versions are added on top of the three.

notes.quote: Because Agnes outraged Anna beyond measure.
notes.reader_gets: "Because" ties Anna's outrage back as the reason she knows every rumour.

notes.quote: Because Agnes outraged Anna beyond measure.
notes.reader_gets: A stiff causal fragment with a bookish intensifier; it reads as translated rather than as a crisp aside.
The binning is an extra reason that sharpened her outrage.
These are study paperwork.
The sheets are for optional courses.

notes.quote: which Agnes had assigned to torment Theodore
notes.reader_gets: Agnes herself set the paperwork in order to torment him.
She is named by her office at the moment of the binning.

notes.quote: with a flick of her golden nails
notes.reader_gets: The gold nails from paragraph 2 do the dismissing.

notes.quote: Theodore's reports and the elective enrollment sheets, which Agnes had assigned to torment Theodore, to Anna's great displeasure, the curator simply swept into the wastebasket
notes.reader_gets: The papers hang as a fronted object through a long aside before the subject and verb arrive; the reader has to reread to see who did what.

notes.quote: swept into the wastebasket with a flick of her golden nails
notes.reader_gets: A natural, vivid gesture.

notes.quote: in Agnes's office, she and Theodore were discussing Anna's future
notes.reader_gets: Probably Agnes and Theodore, but "she" follows a sentence about Anna and could be read as Anna, so it takes a moment to settle.
"Even" makes her ignorance pointed and wry.
Her not knowing answers her knowing every rumour.

notes.quote: Because right now, in Agnes's office, she and Theodore were discussing
notes.reader_gets: A causal fragment with "right now" in past narration and phrases stacked before the subject; stiff and translated.
Anna wants to improve the cosmic Planes of the book's universe.
"Planes" and "plan" in the closing line sit one letter apart, so the echo is visible.
It matches "Planes" in paragraph 18, but paragraph 8 says "Plans", so the term is not held consistently across all three spots.
Her eagerness is stressed, with a note of indulgent scepticism.
Her wealth is framed as an investable asset base.
Anna is aiming for the medical department as her specialisation.

notes.quote: To do good, if she wants so badly to make the Planes better,
notes.reader_gets: The meaning is clear, but the bare purpose fragment standing on its own sounds written rather than spoken.
Unlike Anna, he had no plan for his future.

notes.quote: Nor any place in the Plans.
notes.reader_gets: It reads mainly as no place in anyone's plans; only the capital letter faintly hints at the cosmic Planes of paragraph 7.

notes.quote: Plan. Nor any place in the Plans
notes.reader_gets: The same word, Plan/Plans, links the two lacks.
"Plans" does not match "Planes" in paragraphs 7 and 18, so the callback to the cosmic order is lost.
The emphatic restated name sets him against Anna.
The pronoun immediately restated by the name is a translated-sounding doubled subject.

notes.quote: Helping the Seraphic economy even less.
notes.reader_gets: The refusal carries forward: he does not want to help the economy.
He wants this even less than doing good.

notes.quote: Helping the Seraphic economy even less.
notes.reader_gets: Understandable, but a verbless fragment ending on "even less" sounds slightly off in English.

notes.quote: I don't want to do good.
notes.reader_gets: "Do good" echoes his advice to Anna, so he declines for himself what he urged on her.
She teases him for supposedly weighing an act for someone else's benefit.
The jab is framed by whom the act serves, which his reply at 13 can echo.

notes.quote: Anna can afford to do whatever she likes.
notes.reader_gets: A flat statement about Anna, with no contrastive wording setting her against Theodore.
Her means cover the cost of any choice, matching the "afford" refrain.

notes.quote: Don't tell me you actually considered doing something not for yourself
notes.reader_gets: A quick, amused teasing aside.

notes.quote: The magess sat on the windowsill of her office
notes.reader_gets: Agnes, the magess, is sitting on her own windowsill.
The pointer is made of costly mahogany.

notes.quote: She held the cigarette with telekinesis, and the smoke curled into odd spirals, drifting out of the office into the morning sky and leaving not a drop of smell behind.
notes.reader_gets: The picture comes through, but "held ... with telekinesis", the trailing -ing clauses and "not a drop of smell" read as translated.

notes.quote: Not that there was anything in the office
notes.reader_gets: A wry afterthought: the precaution was hardly needed.
The rapier is made of flysteel, an exotic in-world metal.
Their sessions are named with a worldly, faintly intimate French term.

notes.quote: claiming he needed curating least of all
notes.reader_gets: The reason is clearly Agnes's own claim.
"Curating" echoes her post as curator.
He needs her least of all her students.

notes.quote: she gave it everything she had
notes.reader_gets: She puts in maximal effort.

notes.quote: Agnes said this was how she relaxed during her tête-à-têtes with Theodore, claiming he needed curating least of all.
notes.reader_gets: A smooth report of her breezy excuse.

notes.quote: In truth, she gave it everything she had.
notes.reader_gets: A crisp corrective punchline.

notes.quote: For myself, I'd have left the Academy long ago
notes.reader_gets: "For myself" can be heard as "speaking for myself" rather than "if I acted in my own interest", so the retort to Agnes's jab is blurred.
His reserve option is framed as a plan, echoing Anna's plan and his missing Plan.

notes.quote: I'd have left the Academy long ago
notes.reader_gets: He would have left long since; it is an old, settled wish.

notes.quote: could no longer afford to leave
notes.reader_gets: The barrier is financial, not self-restraint or a ban.
"Afford" repeats the page's refrain of what one's means allow, here negated.
Leaving was once possible and no longer is.
The price is in etons, the same coins as Agnes's melted-down nails.

notes.quote: And so at the entrance exams
notes.reader_gets: The fight follows from the high cost.

notes.quote: not only for a place at the Academy but for the Royal Grant
notes.reader_gets: The grant is a stake on top of admission.

notes.quote: the Royal Grant. The Academician's Golden Card.
notes.reader_gets: The fragment renames the grant as the Golden Card.
The card bears the same title, Academician, as the elite in paragraph 18.

notes.quote: Which covered not only tuition but also the cost of living in Seraph, utterly beyond the means of a sub-seraph or a soul from the Firmament.
notes.reader_gets: A deliberate fragment that clearly continues from the Card.
A coined class term built on the city's name.
The card's spending ceiling grows.
Growth is tied to the Academy's circles.
A grander, more lavish life comes through, but "footing" is a dated, slightly odd choice for free spending.
The lifestyle keeps rising with the limit.
The fees keep getting more expensive.

notes.quote: letting you live in Seraph on an ever grander footing and pay ever costlier tuition fees
notes.reader_gets: Paying rising fees is deadpanned as one more perk.
"Academy residents" could be anyone living at the Academy; the link to the graduated resident mages of paragraph 2 is faint.

notes.quote: even such expenses as designer outfits and cozy houses
notes.reader_gets: "Even" marks clothing and houses as the surprising far end of what the Card covered.

notes.quote: you might never have to pay interest
notes.reader_gets: Staying exempts you from paying interest.

notes.quote: you might never have to pay interest
notes.reader_gets: The exemption is stated flatly; nothing marks it as the surprising peak of the perks.
The exemption could last forever.

notes.quote: And as long as you stayed at the Academy, you might never have to pay interest on a debt that grew endlessly.
notes.reader_gets: A natural English statement of the rule.

notes.quote: on a debt that grew endlessly
notes.reader_gets: "A debt" arrives as new and indefinite; only context links it to the Card's spending.
The debt keeps on growing without stopping.

notes.quote: on a debt that grew endlessly
notes.reader_gets: The twist is left unannounced for the reader to infer.
Nothing in Seraph comes without a price.
The line explains why the debt exists.
The rule is absolute and emphatic.

notes.quote: The only problem was staying at the Academy.
notes.reader_gets: Staying is deadpanned as the sole, seemingly small catch.
A mild, shrugging concession.
The stages are circles, the same ladder as elsewhere.

notes.quote: you could say goodbye to any hope of paying off your debts
notes.reader_gets: From the fourth circle on, the debts can never be repaid; hope is lost.

notes.quote: Which wasn't so easy: from the second circle on, a mage could already work in full; from the fourth, however, you could say goodbye to any hope of paying off your debts.
notes.reader_gets: Understandable, but "work in full", the mid-clause "however" and the switch from "a mage" to "you" make it read as translated.

notes.quote: the mysteries of the Planes, nor poetry, nor metaphysical walks along the thin layers of the True Plane
notes.reader_gets: Both are cosmic levels of existence.
"Thin" reads mostly as physical thinness; only faintly as rarefied or immaterial.
It is a matter of means, echoing the "afford" refrain.
"Only" restricts these pursuits to that group.
Seraph keeps them, that is, supports them; a faintly deflating note.

notes.quote: Only accredited Academicians kept by Seraph could afford those.
notes.reader_gets: A clean closing sentence.
The list is offered as the obvious, shrugging explanation.
The job is deliberately making demons suffer, close kin to "torment" in paragraph 5.

notes.quote: Fight the Disorder, patching holes in the fabric of creation
notes.reader_gets: The stakes are cosmic: holes in creation itself.
The method is humble patch-up work.

notes.quote: Pick through what the scavengers had gathered from the Shards
notes.reader_gets: Scavengers gather; the mage sorts through their haul.

notes.quote: Pick through what the scavengers had gathered from the Shards for treasures, or at least LED bulbs.
notes.reader_gets: "For treasures" lands after "from the Shards" and can briefly attach to the gathering, so the sentence reads a little clumsily.
The bulbs are what you settle for.
Cheap modern electric bulbs.
Hearts are cut out of the dead.
The potions are general healing potions.
Agnes herself holds a silence.
A wink: the pause lasted as long as the narrator's background info-dump.
A kitchen image of Theodore steeping in his prospects.
Theodore torments himself; Agnes merely lets him.
An involuntary, failed exit.

notes.quote: before even reaching the fifth circle
notes.reader_gets: He would fall short of even the fifth circle.
The same circle term as the earlier paragraphs.

notes.quote: Agnes waited out a pause long enough for exposition
notes.reader_gets: The wink lands, but a pause "waited out" like an object with a sufficiency phrase hung on it is a little stiff.
